clue.text: Genial top man-one in the black

indicators.note: the commanding officer and the one sit inside the word for black

parts.note: sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black
OC, Officer Commanding, is the man at the top of a unit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A friendly boss who is also financially solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the black' suggests being out of debt, but it holds SABLE, the heraldic black, around OC and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and enjoys company, which is what being sociable means.

clue.text: Heavy wild dog occupying an animal enclosure

indicators.note: the scrambled dog takes up residence inside the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: wild says the letters of dog run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A savage dog has got into a pigpen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns DOG into ODG, which 'occupying' puts inside STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is dense and filling, a synonym for heavy fare.

clue.text: Advances can be arranged by many branches

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
limbs are the big branches of a tree

explanation.surface: Progress can be organised by numerous departments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be arranged by' only joins the pieces; nothing is anagrammed. 'Advances' is a verb: goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go upward or make progress, a synonym for advancing.

clue.text: Some Arab nervously holding an American

indicators.note: Some says only part of the following letters is wanted
the two words hold the answer inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: An anxious Arab clutching a man from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'holding an American' as the definition, but 'holding' is the second hiding signal; the definition is just 'an American', Abner being the hillbilly of the US comic strip Li'l Abner.
explanation.definitionFit: Abner is a typically American first name, borne by the comic-strip character Li'l Abner.

clue.text: Clearing the member pocket inga fastener

indicators.note: the limb takes the other pieces into itself as a pocket would

parts.note: a leg is a member, that is a limb, of the body
a pin fastens things together

explanation.surface: Someone vaulting over an obstacle while slipping a pin into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'pocketing a' together wrongly; 'pocketing' puts A PIN inside LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a fence or gap means jumping over it, which is what leaping does.

clue.text: A singer in a trio?

parts.note: a high boy's voice, but also a word meaning threefold, so a member of a group of three

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a boy soprano and triple, so the question mark hints at a three-part thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano is called by this term, which also means threefold, hence fitting a trio.

clue.text: Giving a grunt, pen letters, finding it distasteful

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are to be rewritten in another order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling while writing correspondence because they hate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' tells you to rework the letters of A GRUNT PEN; 'Giving' and 'finding it' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is offensive and arouses disgust, hence distasteful.

clue.text: Try as he may, he just can't settle

definitions.text: Try as he may, he just can't settle

parts.words: Try as he may, he just can't settle
parts.note: reads as a restless person but means someone unable to settle his debts

explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' means pay up, not calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A person declared insolvent cannot pay off what is owed to creditors.

clue.text: Caught in the finish, earns way out

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the word for finish

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: way out suggests the letters are wildly displaced

explanation.surface: A runner caught at the finishing line as earnings go astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' turns EARNS into SNARE, which 'in' puts inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ensnared has been trapped, a synonym for caught.

clue.text: Japanese maybe getting into real chaos

indicators.note: chaos means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A visitor from Japan drawn into a real mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins; INTO REAL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese person is an example of an Asian, an Eastern person.

clue.text: Long held by great judges

indicators.note: the yearning is contained within the abbreviation for large

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, so great
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Patience shown by distinguished judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, not an adjective. 'judges' is a verb too: gives a view.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, as one who judges something does.

clue.text: Present from a guy accompanied by a note

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A gift from a man with a note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be in this place, in attendance.

clue.text: Dare begin reforms-that's material

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A challenge to start remaking a garment's fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdine is a tightly woven twill cloth, a type of fabric used for raincoats.

clue.text: A drawback for the Irish police

indicators.note: back means the pair of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: to drag something is to draw or haul it

explanation.surface: A disadvantage facing Ireland's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A DRAG into GARDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the national police force of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Smack which may be seen in East Anglian ports

indicators.note: the letters are visible inside the two words across their join

explanation.surface: A fishing boat spotted in harbours in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' suggests a fishing boat at the ports, but it is a flavour. East Anglia is the region of eastern England round Norfolk and Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack of something is a slight taste or flavour, as is a tang.

clue.text: Nowadays undertaking introduction

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a mission is a task or undertaking

explanation.surface: A modern venture just getting started.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the act of letting someone in, an introduction or entry.

clue.text: Former liberal for instance

parts.note: ex means former
a liberal helping is an ample one

explanation.surface: A one-time Liberal politician cited as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' suggests a party member but means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating something, a synonym for a sample case.

clue.text: A calming influence for the music man?

definitions.text: A calming influence for the music man?

parts.words: A calming influence for the music man?
parts.note: one who composes in the sense of calming, also a writer of music

explanation.walkthrough: To compose oneself is to calm down, so a calmer could be named this.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, and literally is something that composes, that is calms.

clue.text: Ring and ring about the German laying down the law

parts.note: O is a ring shape

indicators.note: the second ring goes around the German article

parts.note: taken as written
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Repeated phone calls about a German official issuing orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Ring' is the letter O; the second is the word itself, put around DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying down the law means giving commands, issuing orders to others.

clue.text: They always row when they get together

definitions.text: They always row when they get together

parts.words: They always row when they get together
parts.note: row reads as quarrel but means pulling oars, done by a crew assembling in a boat

explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow in the surface, but means propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a crew propel a boat by pulling oars together.

clue.text: Prison is the very devil!

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests prison is hell; both halves are definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a jail or police station; also, as Old Nick, the Devil.

clue.text: Attractive, having reduced by a quarter

parts.note: cut means reduced
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Something appealing that has been cut down by a fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' is a compass point, not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means pretty in an endearing way, a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Delude kind associate

parts.note: to con is to deceive
a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: Deceive a friendly companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a companion or partner, someone you associate with.

clue.text: Take industrial action to make an impression

definitions.meaning: to walk out from work in protest
to hit or stamp, as a coin is minted

explanation.walkthrough: Coins are struck, so the second sense is about stamping.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers walk out in protest; and a die stamps a coin's design by hitting it.

clue.text: Stick a number on 11 down

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
the answer to that clue, meaning present

explanation.surface: Fix a figure to the earlier entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places A D above the other answer in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something.

clue.text: A writer writing metrical lines

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An author composing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Verses are written in metre, lines arranged in rhythmic patterns.

clue.text: Quite happy, though quite possibly not decent

indicators.note: suggests a possible version of the letters that follow, rearranged

explanation.surface: Satisfied, despite perhaps being improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' joins; NOT DECENT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content is being satisfied, quite happy with one's lot.

clue.text: Appearing in rep somewhere in town

indicators.note: the letters show up inside the two words across the join

explanation.surface: An actor performing in a repertory theatre somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is a town in Surrey, England, home of the Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a market town in Surrey, England.

clue.text: Tears back-it shows valour

indicators.note: back means the word for tears is read in reverse

parts.note: rips are tears

explanation.surface: Weeping reveals courage after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' is rips, not crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is courage or mettle, a synonym for valour.

clue.text: Scheme involving pins being inserted in the heart

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the centre

parts.note: core means heart, the centre

indicators.note: involving, in its sense of twisting together, jumbles the letters

explanation.surface: A plot involving sticking pins into the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' turns PINS into NSPI, which 'being inserted in' puts inside CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot secretly with others, a synonym for scheming.

clue.text: Soldiers with 27 across preceding a monarch

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
that answer, spirit, and gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Troops with courage ahead of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preceding' just keeps order. 27 across's answer means spirit, and gin is a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, the title of a reigning female monarch.

clue.text: The flight impressed 9 across

parts.note: stamped means impressed, marked by pressing
that answer means Eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: The aircraft impressed the Japanese.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across means Eastern, abbreviated to E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a mass panicked flight of animals or people.
